title: Knowledge check: Dependency Security

questions.prompt: Which principle best guides a correct implementation of dependency security?
options: Load multiple library copies and rely on whichever one executes last.

Accessible interactions use semantic elements, keyboard controls, visible focus, meaningful status updates, and synchronized ARIA state. Secure interfaces render untrusted data safely and rely on server controls for sensitive actions.
Skip error handling and assume the default browser state is always correct.
Render user-controlled strings as HTML so the browser can infer their meaning.
questions.answer_key: Accessible interactions use semantic elements, keyboard controls, visible focus, meaningful status updates, and synchronized ARIA state. Secure interfaces render untrusted data safely and rely on server controls for sensitive actions.
questions.explanation: Accessible interactions use semantic elements, keyboard controls, visible focus, meaningful status updates, and synchronized ARIA state. Secure interfaces render untrusted data safely and rely on server controls for sensitive actions. Apply this principle with the API/version documentation linked in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which check is most useful after trying selecting maintained dependencies?
options: Use a removed jQuery API as the default for new code.
Assume the first attempt succeeded and skip verification.
Use selecting maintained dependencies deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
Bind another global handler after every render without cleanup.
questions.answer_key: Use selecting maintained dependencies deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
questions.explanation: A focused observation checks behavior rather than assuming the method call guarantees the intended result. Include an edge case when the state or inputs can vary.

questions.prompt: Which verification approach best supports professional work with dependency security?
options: Test only the first render and publish immediately.
Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
Move answer keys and private configuration into frontend code.
Replace all native browser APIs with jQuery whether needed or not.
questions.answer_key: Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
questions.explanation: Expected-versus-actual checks, relevant edge cases, and recorded limitations make the implementation easier to debug and review.
